definitions.type: real Euclidean vector space with measure
definitions.definition: V=R^n, realized as tuples (x_1,...,x_n). Its topology is the Euclidean topology and its measure dx is the product of n one-dimensional Lebesgue measures. Compactness, continuity and derivatives use these topologies; integrable means Lebesgue absolutely integrable.

W=R^m with inner product v·w=sum_{k=1}^m v_k w_k and norm |v|=(sum_{k=1}^m v_k^2)^(1/2). On V the same convention uses n coordinates. The squared norm and dot product in all formulas have this meaning.

u_t(x,r) is the derivative at r of the one-variable map ρ↦u(x,ρ). Derivatives are ordinary Fréchet derivatives in coordinate directions; outside their differentiability set use the total derivative convention zero. This convention grants no differentiability.

definitions.type: family indexed by j=1,...,n of functions V×(0,∞)→W
definitions.definition: u_j(x,r)=∂_{x_j}u(x,r), the coordinate derivative in the jth spatial direction.

definitions.type: family indexed by j=1,...,n of functions V×(0,∞)→W
family indexed by j=1,...,n of functions V×(0,∞)→W
definitions.definition: u_jt(x,r)=∂_{x_j}u_t(x,r). Commutation with ∂_r u_j is a claim to be proved, not part of this definition.
Δu(x,r)=sum_{j=1}^n u_jj(x,r), component by component. The gradient D_x u has columns u_j; its Frobenius square is sum_{j=1}^n |u_j|^2.
e_t(x,r)=∂_r e(x,r), with the total derivative convention of D003.

definitions.definition: B_j(x,r)=u_j(x,r)·u_jt(x,r). The symbol B denotes this whole family, not a bound constant.

Let X carry a measurable structure and a topology with every open set measurable, let Z be a normed additive commutative group, let μ be a measure on X finite on compact sets, and let φ:X→Z. If φ is continuous and the closure of {z∈X:φ(z)≠0} is compact (HasCompactSupport), then φ is Bochner integrable with respect to μ.

output.statement: For every t0>0 there exist a compact C⊂V and R>0 such that, with J=[t0/2,3t0/2] and Q=[−R,R]^n, C⊂(−R,R)^n, u(x,r)=q for x∉C and r∈J, and every positive-order coordinate partial derivative of u is zero on (V\C)×int J. For each r∈int J the sections of e,e_t,A,B_j,T_j,g_j and ∂_{x_j}g_j (1≤j≤n) are continuous, vanish outside C, have compact support, and are Lebesgue integrable on V. Each is bounded in absolute value on Q and its absolute integral is at most its bound times |Q|. The box Q is compact, measurable, has Lebesgue measure (2R)^n<∞, and C⊂int Q, so all these sections vanish on a neighborhood of ∂Q. In particular e(·,r) is integrable for every r>0.

locals.declaration: Apply H006 to the positive endpoints t0/2<3t0/2 and choose its compact set C.

argument.text: Fix t0>0 and put J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. Its endpoints satisfy 0<t0/2<3t0/2, so H006 supplies a compact spatial set C on whose complement u=q for every time in J. Compact sets in Euclidean space are closed; hence (V\C)×int J is open. At each of its points u agrees with the constant q on a neighborhood. Every positive-order derivative is therefore zero there: difference quotients of a locally constant function are zero, and this applies successively to all orders. H002 gives continuity of all derivatives on the entire open domain.
Apply M009 to the compact set C and the identity map V→V. The identity is continuous, so it gives a real uniform norm bound even when C is empty.

produces.statement: There exists a real L with |x|≤L for all x∈C.

argument.text: Choose L with the bound of F001 and set R=max(L,0)+1>0 and Q=[−R,R]^n. For x∈C, every coordinate satisfies |x_j|≤|x|≤L<R, so C⊂(−R,R)^n=int Q. H001 gives positive finite dimensions; Q is a compact measurable coordinate box. M010 with all lower endpoints −R and upper endpoints R gives |Q|=∏_{j=1}^n(2R)=(2R)^n<∞.

produces.statement: R>0, Q=[−R,R]^n is compact and measurable, C⊂int Q, |Q|=(2R)^n<∞, and all positive-order derivatives of u vanish on (V\C)×int J.

argument.text: Fix r∈int J. Smoothness in H002 and the finite component formulas defining e,A,B_j,T_j,g_j imply continuity of these functions and of e_t and ∂_{x_j}g_j. The zero derivatives proved in S001 make all of these sections zero outside C. Their nonzero sets have closures contained in the closed compact set C, so each has compact support. Apply M003 to each section with X=V, Z=R and μ=dx: Euclidean Borel open sets are measurable, and Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets. Thus every listed section is integrable. Apply M009 on Q to each continuous scalar section to obtain a finite absolute bound on Q; together with zero values off Q, the usual absolute integral bound is that constant times |Q|. This also proves the supplied bounded-support estimate.

produces.statement: For every ρ∈int J, all sections e(·,ρ), e_t(·,ρ), A(·,ρ), B_i(·,ρ), T_i(·,ρ), g_i(·,ρ), ∂_{x_i}g_i(·,ρ), for 1≤i≤n, are continuous, compactly supported in C, integrable, and have an absolute integral bounded by a finite uniform-in-space bound times |Q|.

argument.text: Since V\C is open and contains ∂Q, every section in F003 vanishes on a neighborhood of ∂Q. The time t0 belongs to int J, so e(·,t0) is integrable. Generalize over the arbitrary t0. The same argument supplies the complete existential common-support assertion and all the asserted bounds for each t0; in particular it proves integrability at every positive time.
